picks.name: juicy-gcode
picks.what: Command-line SVG-to-G-code converter with good Bezier handling and a configurable flavor for pen plotters.

picks.name: svg2gcode
picks.what: Convert paths in SVG files to GCode for a pen plotter, laser engraver, or other machine.

picks.name: svg2gcode
picks.what: Convert SVG to Gcode

picks.name: svg-to-gcode
picks.what: Convert SVG files to G-code for plotter

picks.name: grbl
picks.what: The classic G-code motion controller firmware for the ATmega328 (Arduino Uno). Runs a small CNC/plotter/laser from G-code.

picks.name: Marlin
picks.what: The dominant 3D-printer/CNC firmware; also drives plotters and laser rigs. Heavier than GRBL but very capable.

picks.name: FluidNC
picks.what: Modern GRBL-style firmware for the ESP32 with Wi-Fi, a web UI, and config.yaml. Great if you want wireless control.

stages.capability: host / G-code sender (streams G-code over USB)

picks.name: Universal Gcode Sender (UGS)
picks.what: Cross-platform Java host that streams G-code to GRBL/TinyG/FluidNC over USB, with jogging, visualizer, and macros.

picks.name: CNCjs
picks.what: A web-based G-code sender/controller (Node.js) for GRBL/Smoothie/TinyG; runs in the browser, great on a Raspberry Pi.

picks.name: bCNC
picks.what: Python/Tk GRBL sender with a strong toolpath editor, autoleveling, and G-code utilities.

picks.name: gcode-preview
picks.what: Preview a 3d print from a gcode file

stages.query: arduino cnc shield a4988 stepper driver power supply usb

picks.name: CNC Shield V3 (GRBL-compatible)
picks.what: Plugs onto the Arduino Uno; holds the stepper driver modules and breaks out endstop/spindle pins.

picks.name: A4988 stepper driver module (or DRV8825)
picks.what: One driver per stepper; sets microstepping and current. Buy a spare.

picks.name: 12V/24V 5A DC power supply
picks.what: Powers the motors and drivers. 12V is fine for a small plotter; 24V for a laser.

picks.name: Arduino Uno R3 (or compatible clone)
picks.what: The microcontroller board that runs GRBL firmware. A clone works fine.

stages.capability: motion + frame (steppers, belts, linear motion, structure)
stages.query: nema17 stepper gt2 belt linear rod rail extrusion frame

picks.name: GT2 timing belt + 20T pulleys + idlers kit
picks.what: Converts stepper rotation into linear motion of each axis.

picks.name: 8mm smooth rod + LM8UU linear bearings set
picks.what: The linear guides the carriages ride on. (MGN12 linear rails are a smoother, pricier upgrade.)

picks.name: NEMA17 stepper motor (1.8°, ~0.4-0.5 Nm, e.g. 17HS4401)
picks.what: The two axis motors that move the tool head. One per axis.

picks.name: 2020 aluminium extrusion frame set (~1.5m + brackets)
picks.what: The rigid structure. A laser-cut ply or 3D-printed frame is a cheaper alternative.

stages.capability: tool head + sensors (pen lift or laser, endstops)
stages.query: servo pen lift diode laser module endstop limit switch

picks.name: SG90 / MG90S micro servo (pen lift)
picks.what: Raises and lowers the pen between strokes. Cheapest tool head to start with.

picks.name: Mechanical endstop / limit switch (pack)
picks.what: Homing switches so the machine knows where each axis starts.

picks.name: Diode laser module 10W (optional tool head, PWM/TTL)
picks.what: Optional upgrade to engrave/cut. DANGEROUS — see the safety section. Skip for a first build.
